newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil proposes solution to farm debt paper.
newsitem.headline: Brazil proposes solution to farm debt paper.

text.p: Brazilian President Fernando Henrique Cardoso signed a decree that could speed agrarian reform and offer a deal for holders of special farm debt paper, a Finance Ministry spokesman said.

The spokesman said he did not yet know details of the farm debt deal, but he noted that it sought to resolve the problem of Agrarian Debt Paper, known as TDAs, issued by the government's land reform agency INCRA up to 1992. He said the paper now trades in the market at a considerable discount.
The spokesman said he did not know the total face value of the paper to be covered under the deal.

The decree signed by Cardoso also raises taxes on unproductive land to a maximum of 20 percent of the property's value and also allows the government to confiscate land when owners fail to pay the tax.
The measure is aimed at speeding up the process of agrarian reform, seen as one of Brazil's most serious social problems.
